plan_a_advantages: Includes a tempo run to improve lactate threshold and running speed.
Incorporates a long run to build endurance and trail-specific durability.
Provides a more varied training stimulus, promoting well-rounded development.
plan_b_advantages: Higher volume of easy running may contribute to a stronger aerobic base.
The focus on trail running throughout the week may improve trail-specific skills and confidence.
reasoning: Plan A is the better choice for an athlete aiming to become a faster trail runner. While both plans incorporate rest days and easy runs, Plan A includes a tempo run and a long run, which are crucial for developing speed and endurance – key components of trail running performance. Plan B focuses almost exclusively on easy runs, which, while important for base building, won't sufficiently challenge the athlete to improve speed or trail-specific durability. The structured progression in Plan A, with its inclusion of higher intensity workouts, is more likely to lead to tangible improvements in the athlete's goal.
